subject: helicopter
inspection_scope: Stills only: actually viewed source-keys.png, design.png, and revisions/keys-v1.png; read source.json. Four keys read chronologically top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. No playback inspected.

exact_key_evidence.evidence: Candidate correctly starts with a large right-facing helicopter whose tail is cut by the left edge. Main rotor/mast, tail, and two skid supports attach to the body.

Source is still a close pass: tail exits the left edge and the nose/cabin reaches beyond the right edge. Candidate instead shows the complete tail rotor, tail, cabin and nose within the panel, already reduced to a fully visible aircraft.

Source and candidate both reveal a complete smaller helicopter with a long tail extending left and nose to the right. Candidate preserves the angular nose/window, long single-outline tail and simple skid vocabulary.

Both place a much smaller aircraft toward the right above a low horizon. Candidate remains recognizably the same helicopter with attached rotor, tail and skid, although smooth flight or rotor continuity cannot be established from these stills.

main_gap: Key 2 begins recession and reveals the whole helicopter too early; the source remains a close, doubly cropped pass at that time.
one_bounded_repair: Reframe key 2 alone so the helicopter stays at the source close-pass scale and horizontal placement, with the tail cropped left and nose cropped right; preserve the existing aircraft geometry and leave the later recession intact.
protected_strengths: Coherent aircraft identity and sparse angular cockpit, tail, rotor and skid shapes.
Mechanically readable attachment of mast, tail and skid supports.
Correct right-facing close-to-distant progression in keys 1, 3 and 4, including the late low horizon.
